name: Antidiskriminierungsstelle des Bundes
description: Federal information and counselling resource for people experiencing discrimination or sexual harassment.

name: Berlin State Office for Equal Treatment and Against Discrimination (LADS)
description: Berlin's state anti-discrimination office. Provides information on equal-treatment law, discrimination, publications and Berlin's anti-discrimination work, and connects readers to contact and advisory infrastructure.

name: Deutsches Institut für Menschenrechte
description: Germany's independent national human rights institution, with research, monitoring, documentation and human-rights education.

name: Bundeszentrale für politische Bildung
description: Public political-education resources on democracy, government, fundamental rights, history and current political questions.

name: Amadeu Antonio Stiftung
description: Supports democratic civil society and people confronting racism, antisemitism and right-wing violence and extremism.

name: PRO ASYL
description: Information, advocacy and contact options concerning asylum and refugee rights in Germany and Europe.

name: TelefonSeelsorge Deutschland
description: Free, anonymous crisis and emotional support by telephone, chat and email, available day and night. Phone numbers confirmed on the federal Familienportal on 28 Oct 2026.

name: Verbraucherzentrale
description: Consumer information and counselling through Germany's state consumer centres.

name: Legal Defense Fund
description: Civil-rights legal organization advancing racial justice, voting rights, education equity, economic justice and criminal-justice reform.

name: American Civil Liberties Union
description: Civil-liberties organization with practical Know Your Rights material, including voting and discrimination resources.

name: Equal Justice Initiative
description: Works against racial and economic injustice, excessive punishment and mass incarceration while documenting America's history of racial injustice.

name: Library of Congress: African American History Online
description: Research guide connecting readers to digitized primary sources documenting more than 400 years of African American experience.

name: National Archives: African American Heritage
description: Federal archival records and research guides covering slavery, Reconstruction, civil rights, voting rights and the broader Black experience.

name: FOIA.gov
description: Official federal guide for requesting records from executive agencies under the Freedom of Information Act.

name: National Labor Relations Board: Employee Rights
actions: File or research a labor charge
description: Official information about protected concerted activity, organizing and federal labor-law rights for covered employees.

name: U.S. Department of Labor: Wage and Hour Division
description: Official federal wage-and-hour enforcement resource, including minimum wage, overtime and retaliation information.

name: OSHA Whistleblower Protection Program
description: Official information about retaliation protections administered by OSHA under multiple federal statutes.

name: §14 SGB I — Anspruch auf Beratung
description: German Social Code provision giving everyone a right to advice about rights and duties under the Social Code.

name: §25 SGB X — Akteneinsicht
description: German social-administrative provision governing file inspection by participants in covered proceedings.

name: Betriebsverfassungsgesetz
description: Official text of Germany's Works Constitution Act, including works-council eligibility, complaint rights and co-determination provisions.

name: U.S. Commission on Civil Rights — Complaint Referral
description: Independent federal civil-rights watchdog. Investigates and reports on civil-rights issues; its referral service helps locate complaint offices. It does not represent complainants or enforce remedies.

name: U.S. Department of Justice — Civil Rights Reporting
description: Official portal to report possible federal civil-rights violations, including discrimination and certain law-enforcement misconduct. Reporting does not guarantee investigation, representation, or compensation.

name: Oversight.gov — Federal Inspectors General
description: Search federal inspector-general audits and investigations and find reporting channels. Inspectors general can investigate and recommend action but generally cannot award individual damages.

name: GAO FraudNet — Report Federal Waste or Abuse
actions: Report suspected federal fraud or misuse
description: Receives allegations involving federal funds, waste, abuse and mismanagement, and refers appropriate matters. Not an individual civil-rights compensation or legal representation service.

name: Government Accountability Office — Reports
description: Congressional audit agency documenting federal program performance, failures and recommendations. Its reports are evidence for accountability, not binding awards of compensation.

name: Brennan Center for Justice
description: Nonpartisan law and policy institute researching democracy, voting rights, justice systems and government reform. Not a general individual complaint-resolution service.

name: Project On Government Oversight (POGO)
description: Independent nonprofit watchdog investigating federal misconduct, waste, conflicts of interest and oversight failures. Not a court or compensation agency.

name: ProPublica — Investigative Journalism
description: Independent nonprofit newsroom investigating abuses of power and public-interest failures. Reporting can expose wrongdoing but cannot compel legal remedies.

name: Leadership Conference on Civil and Human Rights
description: Coalition advocating for civil and human rights legislation, enforcement and accountability. Advocacy and policy work are not a substitute for legal representation.

name: NAACP — Civil Rights Advocacy
description: Civil-rights membership organization working on racial justice, voting, education and public accountability. Local assistance and legal referrals vary.

name: TrueVote
actions: Review money, voting records and disclosures
description: Independent third-party research resource for reviewing federal candidates and elected officials through campaign-finance information, congressional activity, voting records and financial disclosures. Verify important findings through the linked primary records.

name: U.S. Wage and Hour Division: 2026-1 Tipped Dual Jobs Bulletin
description: October 19, 2026 federal enforcement guidance withdraws three older opinion letters and confirms that the former 80/20 percentage guidance is not current WHD policy. State law may provide stronger protections.

name: U.S. Department of Labor: State Tipped Minimum Wages
description: Official state-by-state tipped-wage table. Workers should check applicable state and local rules as well as federal tip-credit requirements.

name: IRS: 2025 Adoption Credit Carryforward Adjustment and Penalty Review
description: IRS FAQs explain automatic 2025 adoption-credit adjustments and why an estimated-tax penalty is not automatically recomputed; a separate request may be needed.

name: IRS: IRA Compliance Resolution System (Effective May 2027)
description: IRS October 22, 2026 announcement of a future IRA correction system, with existing automatic waiver and self-certification options remaining available now for qualifying cases.

name: §§2, 38 SGB III: Arbeitsuchendmeldung und Freistellung
actions: Ask employer for time for required appointments
description: German law and Federal Employment Agency guidance on timely job-seeker registration, employer information/release responsibilities and avoiding an ALG I gap.

name: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
description: Free, confidential support if you are in emotional distress or thinking about suicide. Call or text 988, any time. If someone is in immediate danger, call your local emergency number.

name: SAMHSA National Helpline
description: Free, confidential treatment referral and information for mental health and substance use, 24/7, 365 days a year, in English and Spanish. A referral service, not a crisis line.

name: National Problem Gambling Helpline
description: Run by the National Council on Problem Gambling. Offers call, text and chat support around the clock. The current number is on the linked page; check it there before calling.

name: CDC GetTested
description: CDC service for finding nearby places that offer HIV, STI and viral hepatitis testing, plus HPV and hepatitis vaccines, in the United States and its territories.

name: 211 (local help line)
description: Free, confidential referrals to local help with rent or mortgage, utility bills, food, healthcare, childcare and crisis services. The linked page is Central Maryland's service, as an example; dial 211 to reach your local one.

name: Info-Telefon Depression
description: Deutsche Depressionshilfe phone line for people with depression, their relatives and anyone seeking information. Not a 24-hour crisis line.

name: Nummer gegen Kummer
description: Free, anonymous phone counselling for children and young people (116 111) and for parents and other adults worried about a child (0800 111 0 550).

name: Hilfetelefon Gewalt gegen Frauen
description: Free, anonymous support for women who have experienced or are experiencing violence or sexual harassment, and for relatives and professionals.

name: Opfer-Telefon Weisser Ring
description: Free, anonymous phone help for crime victims and their relatives.

name: Deutsche Aidshilfe telephone counselling
description: Anonymous counselling on HIV and other sexually transmitted infections, where to get tested, and PEP. The counselling is free; the call costs 9 cents per minute from German landlines and up to 42 cents from mobiles.

name: Schuldnerberatung finden (BAG Schuldnerberatung)
actions: Find a debt counselling centre by state
description: Directory run by the Bundesarbeitsgemeinschaft Schuldnerberatung to find debt counselling centres in each German state. Check each centre for cost and contact details.

name: Regenbogenportal
actions: Search counselling centres and groups across Germany
Read plain-language guides on law, health and family
description: Information portal of the German federal government on sexual and gender diversity, with a directory of contact points (counselling, groups, anti-discrimination help) across Germany. Run for the Federal Family Ministry; available in several languages. Listing completeness varies by region.

name: LSVD+ – Verband Queere Vielfalt
actions: Request free legal orientation by email
Find counselling run by state associations
description: National LGBTIQ* civil rights association. Offers free first legal orientation by email only (family law, marriage, name and gender entry, asylum, residence; replies can take up to 14 days; no case representation and not for urgent matters). State associations run counselling in some states (e.g. Berlin-Brandenburg, Bavaria, Saxony-Anhalt, Saarland); not every state has it.

name: LSVD+ state associations: counselling overview
description: LSVD+ list of counselling and support services by state, with phone numbers and email for each. Coverage differs by state.

name: Bundesverband Trans*
description: National association of trans* organizations. It does not counsel individuals itself; it trains counsellors and connects member groups across Germany, listed in its member directory.

name: LSBTIQ* counselling centres in North Rhine-Westphalia
actions: Contact one of seven state-funded centres
Counselling for coming-out, violence, relatives, family planning
description: State-funded psychosocial counselling in Bielefeld, Bochum, Dortmund, Köln, Münster and Siegen plus a mobile service for the Niederrhein and western Ruhr. Page published by the NRW family ministry; only for people in NRW.
